standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the hypothesis into the statement that the map from the relation module modulo squares to the free module of differentials is an isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Commutation of tensor products with directed colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used when descending the finitely many elements to a stage (lines 47871-47878)
standard_prerequisites.use: Moves the chosen preimages of the differentials and their relations down to a single index.

core_obligations: Write the presentation of C_0 over B_0 and its base changes at each stage, and record the differential map coming from the presentation over the colimit (proof lines 47857-47871).

Using that the differential is an isomorphism after the colimit, find elements in the relation module over some stage mapping to the differentials and satisfying the relations (proof lines 47871-47878).
Conclude that the base-changed map is etale at that stage (proof lines 47878-47879).
proof_roadmap: Present the algebras and write down the differential isomorphism that etaleness means (proof lines 47856-47871).
Descend the finitely many witnessing elements to one stage and conclude (proof lines 47871-47880).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if a base-changed map of algebras is etale and the source is of finite presentation, then the base-changed map is already etale at some single stage of the colimit (statement lines 47842-47854). The proof does not invoke a general descent theorem for etale maps: it writes explicit presentations, records the differential isomorphism that etaleness amounts to, and then uses that tensor products commute with directed colimits to bring the finitely many witnessing elements, and the relations they satisfy, down to one stage (proof lines 47856-47880). Recognising the hypothesis as finitely many equations, so that it can be descended, is the content of the argument. H2.
